full_target:
Let \(p\) be any prime, \(K\) any field of characteristic \(p\), and
\(\lambda\) an integer with \(0\leq\lambda<p\).
Let \(V(\lambda)\) be the complex irreducible highest-weight
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)\)-module of highest weight \(\lambda\),
of dimension \(\lambda+1\). Its Chevalley generators satisfy

\[
[h,x]=2x,\qquad[h,y]=-2y,\qquad[x,y]=h.
\]

Choose a nonzero highest-weight vector \(v\) with \(xv=0\) and
\(hv=\lambda v\). Let \(U_{\mathbb Z}\) be the integer subalgebra of
the universal enveloping algebra generated by all divided powers
\(X_r=x^r/r!\), \(Y_r=y^r/r!\), for integers \(r\geq0\).
An **admissible lattice** \(M\subset V(\lambda)\) is a free abelian
subgroup with an integer basis that is also a complex basis, stable under
\(U_{\mathbb Z}\). It is arbitrary, not necessarily the minimal lattice.

Put \(V(K)=M\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\). The Lie algebra
\(L(K)=(\mathbb Zx+\mathbb Zy+\mathbb Zh)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\)
acts by the induced lattice operators. This is the Chevalley
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) construction also in characteristic 2.
Prove that \(V(K)\) is nonzero and every \(K\)-linear subspace
invariant under \(x,y,h\) is zero or all of \(V(K)\).
Both \(\lambda=0\) and \(p=2\) are included; \(K\) need not be
algebraically closed.

dependencies.statement: Let K be any field and M any Z-module. There is a unital ring homomorphism ρ:End_Z(M)→End_K(K⊗_Z M) such that ρ(t)(a⊗m)=a⊗t(m) for every t,a,m. It preserves integer multiples as every unital ring homomorphism does, as well as sums, compositions, identity and powers.

lean.type: ∀ (K M : Type*) [Field K] [AddCommGroup M] [Module ℤ M], ∃ ρ : Module.End ℤ M →+* Module.End K (TensorProduct ℤ K M), ∀ (t : Module.End ℤ M) (a : K) (m : M), ρ t (TensorProduct.tmul ℤ a m) = TensorProduct.tmul ℤ a (t m)
lean.proof:
intro K M _ _ _
let ρ : Module.End ℤ M →+* Module.End K (TensorProduct ℤ K M) :=
  { toFun := fun t => t.baseChange K
    map_one' := by exact LinearMap.baseChange_one ℤ M
    map_mul' := by intro f g; exact LinearMap.baseChange_mul f g
    map_zero' := by exact LinearMap.baseChange_zero
    map_add' := by intro f g; exact LinearMap.baseChange_add f g }
refine ⟨ρ, ?_⟩
intro t a m
rfl

dependencies.justification: Native base-change algebra homomorphism contains the proofs preserving all operations; pure-tensor formula is the inspected baseChange_tmul theorem. Restriction of preserving complex maps to M is separately justified by subtype extensionality in R004.

dependencies.statement: Let K be any field, U a finite-dimensional K-vector space and n∈N with dim_K U=n. Suppose F_ij∈End_K(U), indexed by i,j∈Fin n, satisfy F_ij F_kl=(if j=k then F_il else 0) and Σ_i F_ii=Id. Every K-subspace W invariant under all F_ij is zero or U. No positivity hypothesis on n is needed for this dichotomy.

origin.reference: Elementary matrix-unit proof in basis proof R007, from B001

lean.type: ∀ (K U : Type*) [Field K] [AddCommGroup U] [Module K U] [FiniteDimensional K U] (n : ℕ) (F : Fin n → Fin n → Module.End K U), Module.finrank K U = n → (∀ i j k l, F i j * F k l = if j = k then F i l else 0) → (∑ i : Fin n, F i i) = 1 → ∀ W : Submodule K U, (∀ i j (w : U), w ∈ W → F i j w ∈ W) → W = ⊥ ∨ W = ⊤
lean.proof:
classical
intro K U _ _ _ _ n F hdim hmul hsum W hW
by_cases hbot : W = ⊥
· exact Or.inl hbot
right
obtain ⟨w, hw, hw0⟩ := Submodule.exists_mem_ne_zero_of_ne_bot hbot
have hex : ∃ j : Fin n, F j j w ≠ 0 := by
  by_contra hn
  have hz : ∀ j : Fin n, F j j w = 0 := by simpa using hn
  have hs := congrArg (fun f : Module.End K U => f w) hsum
  have : w = 0 := by simpa [LinearMap.sum_apply, hz] using hs.symm
  exact hw0 this
obtain ⟨j, hj⟩ := hex
let u : U := F j j w
have hu0 : u ≠ 0 := hj
have huW : u ∈ W := hW j j w hw
have huu : F j j u = u := by
  have ht := congrArg (fun f : Module.End K U => f w) (hmul j j j j)
  simpa [Module.End.mul_apply, u] using ht
let v : Fin n → U := fun i => F i j u
have hact (k i : Fin n) : F j k (v i) = if k = i then u else 0 := by
  have ht := congrArg (fun f : Module.End K U => f u) (hmul j k i j)
  change F j k (F i j u) = _
  by_cases hki : k = i
  · simpa [Module.End.mul_apply, hki, huu] using ht
  · simpa [Module.End.mul_apply, hki] using ht
have hli : LinearIndependent K v := by
  apply Fintype.linearIndependent_iff.mpr
  intro g hg k
  have ht := congrArg (fun x : U => F j k x) hg
  have hs : g k • u = 0 := by
    simpa [map_sum, map_smul, hact] using ht
  exact (smul_eq_zero.mp hs).resolve_right hu0
have hspan : Submodule.span K (Set.range v) = ⊤ :=
  YuiBasis.B001 K U (Fin n) v hli (by simpa using hdim.symm)
apply top_unique
rw [← hspan]
apply Submodule.span_le.mpr
rintro x ⟨i, rfl⟩
exact hW i j u huW

dependencies.justification: Choose nonzero w∈W, find j with u=F_jj w≠0 from the diagonal sum, and let u_i=F_ij u. Applying F_jk to any linear relation among u_i leaves its k-th coefficient times u, hence all coefficients vanish. B001 with index Fin n gives span(range u_i)=U because dim U=n. Every u_i lies in W, so W=U. The zero-W case is immediate; if n=0 the diagonal sum precludes nonzero w. This is a concrete recursive derivation from B001, and its eventual Lean proof may use only that frozen project premise and native Mathlib.

propositions.statement: p is an arbitrary prime, K is an arbitrary field with Char K=p, and λ is an integer with 0≤λ<p.

V is the complex irreducible highest-weight sl₂(C)-module of highest weight λ and complex dimension λ+1. Its endomorphisms x,y,h satisfy hx−xh=2x, hy−yh=−2y and xy−yx=h. The vector v∈V is nonzero and satisfies xv=0 and hv=λv.

M⊂V is an arbitrary free abelian subgroup with an integer basis which is also a complex basis of V, and M is stable under the integer enveloping subalgebra generated by all X_r=x^r/r! and Y_r=y^r/r! (r∈N). The induced x,y,h actions on V(K)=M⊗_Z K are the actions in the target.

For i=0,…,λ, the vectors e_i=y^iv/i! form a complex basis of V. They satisfy xe_0=0, xe_i=(λ−i+1)e_(i−1) for 1≤i≤λ, ye_i=(i+1)e_(i+1) for i<λ, ye_λ=0, and he_i=(λ−2i)e_i. For every r≥0, X_r e_i=binom(λ−i+r,r)e_(i−r) if r≤i and zero otherwise; Y_r e_i=binom(i+r,r)e_(i+r) if i+r≤λ and zero otherwise.

For i,j∈{0,…,λ}, let E_ij be the complex linear map sending e_j to e_i and every e_k with k≠j to zero, and put c_j=binom(λ,j), A_ij=X_(λ−i)Y_λX_λY_(λ−j), and D=∏_(t=0)^λ c_t. Each A_ij preserves M, A_ij=c_jE_ij, A_ij A_kl=δ_(jk)c_j A_il, and D Id_V=Σ_(i=0)^λ(∏_(t≠i)c_t)A_ii.
For every j with 0≤j≤λ the integer c_j=binom(λ,j) has nonzero image in K; for every r with 0≤r≤λ the integer r! has nonzero image in K. Hence D=∏_(j=0)^λ c_j also has nonzero image in K.

Let A_ij^K denote the operator induced by A_ij|_M on U=M⊗_Z K and define F_ij=(c_j in K)^(-1) A_ij^K for 0≤i,j≤λ. Then F_ij F_kl=δ_(jk)F_il and Σ_(i=0)^λ F_ii=Id_U. For 0≤r≤λ the induced divided powers satisfy (r! in K)X_r^K=(x^K)^r and (r! in K)Y_r^K=(y^K)^r.
The K-vector space U=M⊗_Z K has dimension λ+1, and U≠0.
Every K-linear subspace W⊂U=M⊗_Z K invariant under the induced x,y,h operators is invariant under every F_ij=(binom(λ,j) in K)^(-1)(X_(λ−i)Y_λX_λY_(λ−j))^K for 0≤i,j≤λ.

The vector space V(K)=M⊗_Z K is nonzero, and every K-linear subspace invariant under the induced x,y,h is either zero or all of V(K), for all the original parameters including λ=0, p=2, and arbitrary fields K of characteristic p.
Let K be a field, U a finite-dimensional K-vector space, ι a finite type, and v:ι→U a linearly independent family. If card ι=dim_K U, then span_K(range v)=U.
Let K be any field, M any Z-module, and b a Z-basis of M indexed by an arbitrary type ι. There exists a K-basis B of K⊗_Z M indexed by the same ι with B_i=1⊗b_i.

Let K be any field and M any Z-module. There is a unital ring homomorphism ρ:End_Z(M)→End_K(K⊗_Z M) such that ρ(t)(a⊗m)=a⊗t(m) for every t,a,m. It preserves integer multiples as every unital ring homomorphism does, as well as sums, compositions, identity and powers.
For a prime p, a ring A with CharP A p, and n∈N, the element n! cast to A is a unit if and only if n<p.
For natural numbers n,k with k≤n, choose(n,k)·k!·(n−k)!=n!.
For any field K, K-vector space U, arbitrary index type ι, and basis b:Basis ι K U, dim_K U (the natural finrank) equals Nat.card ι.
For any field K and Z-module M there is an additive equivalence e:M⊗_Z K≃K⊗_Z M satisfying e(m⊗a)=a⊗m. Additivity makes e and its inverse Z-linear automatically.

Let K be any field, U a finite-dimensional K-vector space and n∈N with dim_K U=n. Suppose F_ij∈End_K(U), indexed by i,j∈Fin n, satisfy F_ij F_kl=(if j=k then F_il else 0) and Σ_i F_ii=Id. Every K-subspace W invariant under all F_ij is zero or U. No positivity hypothesis on n is needed for this dichotomy.

proof:
Write λ as a natural number using 0≤λ and put n=λ+1. The original hypotheses H001–H003, including arbitrariness of M and K, remain the only assumptions. We use K⊗_Z M as an optional representation of M⊗_Z K, through the flip m⊗a↦a⊗m; this map and its inverse are well defined by the balanced bilinear relations and intertwine all lattice operators.

R001. Induction using hy−yh=−2y gives hy^iv=(λ−2i)y^iv. Induction using xy−yx=h then gives xy^iv=i(λ−i+1)y^(i−1)v for i≥1: the induction step is x y^(i+1)v=y x y^iv+h y^iv=[i(λ−i+1)+λ−2i]y^iv=(i+1)(λ−i)y^iv. Thus x^iy^iv=i!λ(λ−1)…(λ−i+1)v, nonzero for i≤λ over C. Consequently e_i=y^iv/i! is nonzero. To prove independence, apply ∏_(k≠j)(h−(λ−2k)Id) to a relation Σa_i e_i=0. Every term except j vanishes, while its remaining factor ∏_(k≠j)2(k−j) is nonzero in C. Hence every a_j=0. There are n independent vectors in an n-dimensional space, so they form a basis. The vector y^(λ+1)v has h-weight −λ−2; expansion in the basis and application of h show every coefficient is zero, since −λ−2 differs from all λ−2i. This proves the endpoint ye_λ=0. Division by factorials gives the displayed x,y,h formulas. Repeated application gives the two binomial-coefficient formulas for X_r,Y_r, including zero beyond the endpoints. No assertion about reduced h-eigenvalues is used.

R002. Put P₀=Y_λX_λ. The formulas just proved give P₀=E_(λλ), X_(λ−i)P₀=E_(iλ), and P₀Y_(λ−j)=c_jE_(λj), where c_j=binom(λ,j). Therefore A_ij=X_(λ−i)P₀Y_(λ−j)=c_jE_ij. Each factor preserves M by admissibility, hence so does A_ij. The elementary relations E_ij E_kl=δ_(jk)E_il and ΣE_ii=Id give A_ij A_kl=δ_(jk)c_jA_il and D Id=Σ_i(∏_(t≠i)c_t)A_ii, with D=∏_t c_t. These are identities with integer coefficients between maps preserving M. Products over empty index sets are one.

R003. For 0≤r≤λ<p, every integer 1,…,r is nonzero in K, so r! is nonzero. For j≤λ the integer identity binom(λ,j)j!(λ−j)!=λ!, after casting to K, proves binom(λ,j)≠0. The product D is therefore nonzero. This uses only primality/characteristic and the strict bound λ<p, with no assumption that K is algebraically closed.

R004. Restrict lattice-preserving maps to Z-linear maps on M. Restriction is faithful because M is a subgroup of V. An identity of integer linear combinations and compositions on V therefore remains an identity on M. Extend these restricted maps to K⊗_Z M by a⊗m↦a⊗T(m). The tensor-product universal property gives a unital ring homomorphism from End_Z(M) to End_K(K⊗_Z M): it preserves sums, products, integer scalars and identity, as checked on pure tensors, which span. Transfer back by the tensor flip to U=M⊗_Z K. Thus both identities of R002 hold over K. Setting F_ij=c_j^(-1)A_ij^K gives F_ijF_kl=δ_(jk)F_il. To check ΣF_ii=Id, multiply the transferred identity D Id=Σ_i(∏_(t≠i)c_t)A_ii^K by D^(-1); the coefficient of A_ii^K is c_i^(-1). The same transfer applies to the characteristic-zero identities r!X_r=x^r and r!Y_r=y^r, since both sides preserve M and r! is an integer.

R005. An integer basis m_0,…,m_λ of M extends to a K-basis 1⊗m_0,…,1⊗m_λ of K⊗_Z M. Explicit coordinate maps are a⊗m↦(a·(the integer coordinates of m in K)); their inverse is (a_i)↦Σ_i a_i⊗m_i. These are mutually inverse by the balanced tensor relations. The tensor flip gives a K-basis of U. Hence dim_K U=n>0 and U is nonzero.

R006. If a subspace W is stable under x^K,y^K, it is stable under all their powers. By R003 and R004, X_r^K=(r!)^(-1)(x^K)^r and Y_r^K=(r!)^(-1)(y^K)^r for r≤λ. Thus W is stable under the factors of A_ij^K, their composites, and their scalar multiples F_ij. Invariance under h, supplied by the original target, is allowed and need not be used.

R007. Here is the elementary matrix-unit argument in the needed generality. On any n-dimensional vector space over any field, suppose maps F_ij indexed by Fin n satisfy F_ijF_kl=δ_(jk)F_il and ΣF_ii=Id. Let W be invariant. If W≠0 choose w∈W nonzero. Since w=ΣF_iiw, some u=F_jjw is nonzero. Put u_i=F_iju. All u_i lie in W. For a relation Σa_i u_i=0, applying F_jk gives a_k u=0, because F_jkF_ij=δ_(ki)F_jj and F_jju=u. Thus a_k=0 for every k. The n independent vectors u_i form a basis by the dimension hypothesis; since they lie in W, W is the whole space. Applying this to R004–R006 and the dimension and nonzero result R005 proves P.

Replacement account. The localized arbitrary-lattice argument, its common coordinate module J, the rational rank computation n=nr, valuation/principality of J, and localization/reduction associativity are removed. They are replaced by integer identities among the A_ij, tensor extension of integral endomorphisms, the elementary scalar-extension basis, and the matrix-unit lemma. No standard form of M is asserted. The divided-power normalization, original commutator signs and strict parameter bound are retained. For λ=0 all products are empty or one, P₀=X₀=Y₀=Id, and the argument reduces to a one-dimensional space. For p=2 only λ=0,1 occur and no distinct-weight assertion is made in K.

Selected foundation plan. The complete hard frontier was investigated together. Its proposed full sl2-coordinate package is replaced by the explicit local R001 induction and only the shared finite-dimensional spanning theorem B001 and factorial identity B005. The proposed combined tensor package is split into independent native constructions B002 (basis), B003 (endomorphism homomorphism), B006 (basis cardinality), and B007 (tensor flip). The coefficient argument uses native B004 and B005, and the sole new abstract derived cut is B008, with direct premise B001. All source-backed leaves were inspected in the frozen Mathlib files; public comparison revisions were not substituted for the task pin. No textbook residual, new H, or source-dependent external theorem remains. The given irreducibility over C and [h,x]=2x may remain unused in the elementary coordinate derivation; they are retained as original assumptions. Basis proof preparation and structural validation are separate from the subsequent independent mathematical and application review.
